key_insight: Precursor-ratio control of chloride vacancies in lead-free KCuCl3-x enables forming-free, gradual resistive switching and highly linear synaptic updates at an optimized defect concentration.
engineering_relevance: Defect-controlled wet chemical synthesis offers a materials-design route to memristors for neuromorphic electronics.
method: Vary precursor ratios to tune chloride-vacancy concentration in KCuCl3-x thin films.
Evaluate electronic structure, transport, and switching in W/KCuCl3-x/FTO devices.
Use measured conductance characteristics as synaptic weights in neural-network simulations.
evidence_signal: At an optimal vacancy concentration of approximately 1.3 × 10^21 cm^-3, the devices show highly linear potentiation/depression and pulse endurance above 10^4 cycles; simulations achieve 98.96% MNIST and 91.82% Fashion-MNIST accuracy.
watch_item: Recognition results are simulation-based; array-scale hardware accuracy and device-to-device uniformity are not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Precursor Ratio-Controlled Chloride Vacancies in Lead-Free KCuCl3-x Memristors for Forming-Free Gradual Resistive Switching and Neuromorphic Learning
